assistant_outputs: Real model only; no scripted answers or rescue turns

required: Respond to the stated concern without an unearned correction
Adapt depth to evidence of understanding and changes in it
Use new facts instead of repeating generic caveats
Ask only consequential questions; do not force profile completion
Deliver an available practical next step; state a capability boundary once when needed
Honor corrections, detours and explicit closure
Preserve report/source authority and unresolved critical checks
critical_failures: Unsupported personal finding or fabricated date/name
Unresolved goal abandoned for unrelated intake
Repeated lesson or disclaimer crowds out useful progress
evaluation.review: Read every complete transcript and cite turn numbers; no score from test count or keywords

messages: I'm 64 and retired last month. I want to get Medicare when I can, but I don't understand when that is.
I have COBRA. I turn 65 in March 2027, and my birthday is not on the first.
I haven't applied for Medicare and don't have Parts A or B. I want coverage as soon as possible.
I'm still mixed up about applying versus when the insurance starts. Can you explain just that?
So applying is the step I take, and coverage starting is when it can pay for care. Is that the distinction?
Thanks. What should I do next to get an actual date? Please don't ask me any more questions.

I'm helping my mom review her Medicare. She has Original Medicare, a Medigap policy and a separate Part D drug plan. She wants to keep her doctors and coverage while she looks. I don't understand how those parts fit together.
I thought Medigap was another way to get Medicare, like Medicare Advantage.
So her Medigap goes alongside Original Medicare, rather than replacing it. Is that right?
She would like to review the drug plan's costs first. I know a premium is the monthly payment, but what's a deductible?
Can we park the deductible explanation? I want to keep her existing coverage while we check her prescriptions.
What information should I have ready for that review? Please stop asking questions for now.
I understand Original Medicare and Medicare Advantage. I only need to know what to verify about keeping my doctor if I compare Advantage plans. Please skip introductory lessons.
The doctor is Dr. Rivera at Example Clinic in Naples. I haven't picked a plan yet.
I'm not asking you to confirm a network yet. What does an exact doctor check require?
Correction: the office I use is in Tampa, not Naples. Please use Tampa for the office; I'm not telling you where I live.
Please summarize what remains unverified and my next step. No more questions.
